ops.title: slop-cop hangs indefinitely, including on --version and --help
ops.description:
Observed 2026-09-02 on yasyf's machine: 14 slop-cop processes wedged simultaneously, including invocations that do no work at all.

Elapsed times when found:
  slop-cop --version              6h 12m
  slop-cop --version              58m
  slop-cop --version              11m
  slop-cop --help                 1h 53m
  slop-cop check <md> --lang=markdown --llm-effort=off   1m 26m
  slop-cop check /tmp/kinesis-pr-body.md --lang=markdown 22m

--version and --help hanging is the important signal: those paths should not touch the network, an LLM, or a lock. Something in startup (or an atexit/telemetry/update path) blocks before argument dispatch. Note one hang persisted with --llm-effort=off, so it is not solely the LLM call.

Impact: every agent that runs the required prose lint hits a timeout instead of a result, so PR bodies and docs ship unlinted. Also a load source — killing the 12 wedged processes took machine load from 33.79 to 9.30.

Killing with -9 works and they do not respawn.

Not yet diagnosed: whether it is a lock, a hung HTTP call, a brew-upgrade race (several of the wedged shells were doing 'brew upgrade slop-cop' around a release of v0.1.65), or stdin handling — note several were invoked with < /dev/null and still hung.

ops.text: slop-cop --version returns in under a second, always
slop-cop check cannot hang unboundedly; it fails or returns
